The Tennessee woman who survived a failed execution is now awake, reporter Katherine
Sweeney of member station WPLN reports.
Christa Pike has been hospitalized since Wednesday.
That's when Tennessee tried and failed to put her to death for her role in the 1995
killing of Colleen Slimmer.
The prison administered two doses of lethal drugs, but she ultimately left in an ambulance.
Her attorneys announced Tuesday afternoon she was not only conscious, but speaking.
They said she was handcuffed to her bed, even though her arms are covered in burns and blisters.
They attribute those injuries to bad IV placement during her attempted execution and say it's
likely the Pinto Barbatol intended to kill her flowed into her flesh instead of into
her bloodstream.
For NPR News, I'm Katherine Sweeney in Nashville.
There are just four weeks to go until midterm election day.
More than a million voters have already cast ballots and more than a billion dollars in
political ads are planned across key House and Senate contests.
NPR's Stephen Fowler reports on the political landscape.
The map of races both parties view as competitive is expansive and runs deep into states where
President Trump comfortably won in 2024.
And the House party committees have ID'd close to 100 seats, they feel are in play, with
millions in spending lined up to try and shape the outcome.
And in the Senate, Republicans have pulled back money from Georgia and North Carolina,
where Democrats are pulling better, instead sending resources to places like Kansas and
South Carolina, where Trump's unpopularity makes the midterm more competitive than one
might expect.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
President Trump was asked today about that taxpayer-funded ad campaign headed into the
November midterms.
A day after saying he would now pay for the ads using money from his super back, he did
not commit to reimbursing the billions already spent, telling reporters in his words, "We'll
decide whether to repay the funds."
Federal law enforcement officials are charging a Washington state resident with aiding and
encouraging a school shooter in Canada.
Amy Rado of member station KUOW reports from Seattle.
Federal authorities arrested James Cody Bryant in Bellingham, Washington on a charge of conspiring
to murder persons in a foreign country, in connection with the February 10th school shooting
in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia.
The shooter killed two family members, five children, and a school staff member before
turning the gun on herself.
FBI Special Agent Mike Harrington says Bryant helped the shooter plan in online chats.
"In addition to providing money, technical advice, and particular items to be used in
the shooting, Bryant agreed to record a livestream feed of the attack and broadcast it in a way
that would maximize notoriety for the shooter."
The two met on the online platform Discord, which shared the information with law enforcement.
Prosecutors say the charge is punishable by up to life in prison.
For NPR News, I'm Amy Rado in Seattle.
And you're listening to NPR News.
